title: A scheme carrying an ample invertible module is separated
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal L$ an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $X$ is separated, i.e. the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. (More generally the conclusion holds as soon as every point of $X$ lies in an affine open $X_s$ for some $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge1$; quasi-compactness of $X$ is not used.)

source.place: Properties, Lemma 09MP (label lemma-ample-separated), proved by Lemma 01PY (label lemma-affine-s-opens-cover-quasi-separated) and Definition 01PS

proof.text: *The covering.* Let $\mathcal A$ be the set of pairs $(n,s)$ with $n\ge1$, $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ and $X_s$ an affine open of $X$, where $X_s=\{x\in X:\ s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\}$, equivalently the set of $x$ where the value $s(x)\in(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})(x)=(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)$ is nonzero, as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. By condition (2) of that definition (or by the hypothesis of the more general statement) every $x\in X$ lies in some $X_s$ with $(n,s)\in\mathcal A$, so the affine opens $X_s$, $(n,s)\in\mathcal A$, cover $X$. Condition (1) (quasi-compactness) is not used anywhere below.

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS (definition-ample) (2); proof of Lemma 01PY, first sentence ('By assumption we can find a covering of X by affine opens of the form X_s')

proof.text:
*Bringing two sections to a common degree.* Fix $(p,s),(q,t)\in\mathcal A$ and put $U=X_s$, $V=X_t$, $\mathcal M=\mathcal L^{\otimes pq}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1) and (2) (applied with $f=\mathrm{id}_X$: tensor products of invertible modules are invertible, and the factors of a finite tensor product may be regrouped and reordered by canonical isomorphisms) the $q$-fold tensor power of $\mathcal L^{\otimes p}$ and the $p$-fold tensor power of $\mathcal L^{\otimes q}$ are both canonically isomorphic to $\mathcal M$; let $s'\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ be the image of $s\otimes\cdots\otimes s$ ($q$ factors) and $t'\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ the image of $t\otimes\cdots\otimes t$ ($p$ factors). By part (3) of the same lemma, for $x\in X$ the value of a tensor product of sections is the tensor product of the values, $(u\otimes v)(x)=u(x)\otimes v(x)$ in the tensor product over $\kappa(x)$ of two one-dimensional $\kappa(x)$-vector spaces, which is nonzero iff $u(x)
eq0$ and $v(x)
eq0$; an isomorphism of invertible modules induces an isomorphism on the fibres at $x$, so it preserves (non)vanishing of values. By induction on the number of factors, $s'(x)
eq0$ iff $s(x)
eq0$ and $t'(x)
eq0$ iff $t(x)
eq0$, i.e. $X_{s'}=X_s=U$ and $X_{t'}=X_t=V$ (Stacks 01PT: $X_{s^n}=X_s$). So we may compare $s'$ and $t'$ as sections of the one invertible module $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 01PY, second paragraph ('We now replace s by s^q, t by t^p, and L by L^{pq}. This is harmless as X_s = X_{s^q} and X_t = X_{t^p}'); proof of Lemma 01PT ('X_{s^n} = X_s'); Section 01PR ('X_s cap X_{s'} = X_{ss'}')

proof.text:
*$U\cap V$ is a principal open of $U$ and of $V$.* Write $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $B=\mathcal O_X(V)$, $W=U\cap V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] applied to $(X,\mathcal M,s')$, the open $X_{s'}=U$ carries the isomorphism $\mathcal O_U	o\mathcal M|_U$, $a\mapsto a\,s'|_U$; hence there is a unique $f\in A$ with $t'|_U=f\cdot s'|_U$. Likewise, applied to $(X,\mathcal M,t')$, there is a unique $g\in B$ with $s'|_V=g\cdot t'|_V$. For $x\in U$, taking values at $x$ (the map $\mathcal M(U)	o\mathcal M(x)$ is linear over $A	o\kappa(x)$) gives $t'(x)=f(x)\,s'(x)$ with $s'(x)
eq0$, so $t'(x)
eq0$ iff $f(x)
eq0$. Hence $W=U\cap X_{t'}=\{x\in U: f(x)
eq0\}=D(f)$, the principal open of the affine open $U$ defined by $f$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]; symmetrically $W=D(g)\subseteq V$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CY (lemma-s-open: L|_{X_s} is trivialized by s); Properties, proof of Lemma 01PV (lemma-affine-cap-s-open: U cap X_s is the principal open of U where the coordinate of s is invertible) and proof of Lemma 01PY, first paragraph (the intersection of two affine X_s is affine)

proof.text: *$W$ is affine with ring $A_f$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] (b) applied to the affine open $U$ and $f\in A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, the open $W=D(f)$ is an affine open of $X$ and the restriction $A\to\mathcal O_X(W)$ is a localization of $A$ at $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$: $f|_W$ is a unit and every element of $\mathcal O_X(W)$ is $a|_W\cdot(f|_W)^{-k}$ for some $a\in A$, $k\ge0$.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 01PV (U cap X_s is affine) and proof of Lemma 01PY, first paragraph; Schemes, Lemma 01HS (lemma-standard-open: O(D(f)) = A_f)

proof.text: *Surjectivity of $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B\to\mathcal O_X(W)$.* On $W=U\cap V$ step 3 gives $t'|_W=f|_W\,s'|_W=f|_W\,g|_W\,t'|_W$. Since $W\subseteq V=X_{t'}$ and $a\mapsto a\,t'|_V$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_V\to\mathcal M|_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], the coefficient of $t'|_W$ is unique, so $f|_W\,g|_W=1$ in $\mathcal O_X(W)$, i.e. $(f|_W)^{-1}=g|_W$. By step 4 every element of $\mathcal O_X(W)$ has the form $a|_W(f|_W)^{-k}=a|_W\cdot(g^k)|_W$ with $a\in A$, $g^k\in B$, which is the image of $a\otimes g^k$ under the ring map $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B\to\mathcal O_X(W)$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x|_W\,y|_W$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Hence this map is surjective. (This is the computation of Stacks Constructions 01MC for $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$ in $\operatorname{Proj}$: an element of the intersection is an element of one chart times a power of the inverse of the transition function, which is a function on the other chart.)

source.place: Constructions, proof of Lemma 01MC (lemma-proj-separated: surjectivity of S_(f) (x)_Z S_(g) -> S_(fg)), whose argument is transposed here to the charts X_s, X_t; Schemes, Lemma 01KP (2)(b)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-cover-criterion] to the affine scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and the covering of $X$ by the affine opens $V_{(n,s)}=X_s$, $(n,s)\in\mathcal A$ (step 1): for any two members $X_s,X_t$ the intersection is affine (step 4) and $\mathcal O_X(X_s)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_X(X_t)\to\mathcal O_X(X_s\cap X_t)$ is surjective (step 5). Hence $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], i.e. $X$ is separated. Only the covering hypothesis of step 1 was used, which proves the more general statement as well.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated) (2), as used in Constructions, proof of Lemma 01MC; Properties, Lemma 09MP (lemma-ample-separated: 'Follows immediately from Lemma 01PY and Definition 01PS')

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against Stacks 09MP, 01PY, 01PS). Proof written in 6 steps following the lead's plan: the affine X_s cover X; two sections are brought to the common degree pq (01PY, 01PT, fibre values of tensor products from lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor); X_s cap X_t is the principal open D(f) of X_s, with t'=f s' (lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes), hence affine with ring O(X_s)_f (lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime); fg=1 on the intersection gives surjectivity of O(X_s) (x)_Z O(X_t) -> O(X_s cap X_t); conclude by lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-cover-criterion with S = Spec Z. Stacks itself proves 01PY by the valuative criterion; the route via Schemes 01KP(2) transposes Constructions 01MC and is marked proof_origin agent. No new nodes; quasi-compactness unused. Two cited lemmas (nonvanishing-section-trivializes, invertible-pullback-tensor) are in unit sk-thm-reduction, which sk-thm-p1 does not cite: generic tool uses for the lead to record.
